content: One record per iteration of every database-mode run: the hypothesis Agent 1 produced and the constraints Agent 2 derived from it. This is the reasoning behind each design decision in the paper.

One record per iteration of every discovery-mode run, for all four campaigns: the hypothesis Agent 1 produced and the constraints Agent 2 derived from it, with both the plotted iteration index and the index on disk.
Database-mode campaigns: the per-iteration values recorded for each of the four beams, for nine design tasks in five replicates. This is the quantity the trajectory panels plot.

Database-mode campaigns: per iteration and beam, the median target and the median of every pore descriptor, with the number of matched candidates. These are the points the descriptor-space trajectories plot.

The hypothesis beam placed in the derived electronic space of those panels: per task, replicate and iteration, the mean position on the metal axis and the mean linker conjugation index, with the number of candidates behind each point.
The ordering the metal axis uses, from closed-shell to open-shell, so the panels can be redrawn on the same axis.

The top 100 hypothesis-beam structures per condition, for four database-mode conditions and two discovery-mode conditions, with the pore descriptors the design-space panel plots; the metal counts of panel d are taken over the same sets.
Discovery mode at 160 K and 5 bar, same columns.
Discovery mode at 77 K and 5 bar: every successfully simulated structure with its hydrogen uptake and pore geometry.
Discovery mode for ethane/ethylene selectivity at 298 K and 1 bar: every successfully simulated structure, with the beam that proposed it, the replicate, the iteration and the pore geometry.
Discovery mode for SF6 capture at 298 K and 1 bar, in mol/kg, same columns.

Iterations needed to reach the database top 10%.

Table S2 itself: per task, the top-1% threshold, and for the hypothesis beam and the random baseline the number of proposed candidates that cleared it, the number proposed, the resulting hit rate and the enrichment factor.
Per-task final-iteration database percentile for every backend, with the number of scored replicates.

The nine structures the paper names, as CIFs assembled from the released building-block library: the database-mode winners and the global best of Table S1, and the best structure of each discovery campaign. The hMOF and QMOF winners are public database entries and are cited by their own identifiers.
